Payment providers often need funds available in different markets before international transfers can be completed. Maintaining that liquidity across multiple countries can tie up capital and create operational challenges.

The partnership aims to address this through:
• Short-term RLUSD funding: Licensed payment companies can access funds for cross-border payment flows.
• Flexible capital deployment: Providers can use the funding and typically repay it within one to five days after payments are completed.
• Existing payment activity: Arf reports approximately $10 billion in annual global settlement volume.
• Potential on-chain lending: Arf plans to explore XRPL’s proposed Single Asset Vaults and Lending Protocol as the network’s native lending infrastructure develops.

The proposed lending features must still pass XRPL’s amendment process before launching on the main network.

This partnership highlights how stablecoins such as RLUSD are being explored as tools for payment liquidity, not just as digital assets for trading.

#BTC","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/unocoin_btc-activity-7518948537309716480-9O2T"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"SocialMediaPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Unocoin: Crypto ka Super App","url":"https://in.linkedin.com/company/unocoin"},"datePublished":"2026-10-22T07:26:31.108Z","interactionStatistic":{"@type":"InteractionCounter","interactionType":"http://schema.org/LikeAction","userInteractionCount":0},"mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/unocoin_solana-alpenglow-blockchain-activity-7518935805529153536-WSNp","text":"Solana has activated Alpenglow, its most significant consensus upgrade since 2020.

The mainnet upgrade, activated on October 21, replaces the long-standing TowerBFT consensus system with Votor, a new protocol designed to make transactions final much faster.

Key developments:
• Targeting 150ms finality: The upgrade aims to reduce expected finality from approximately 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds.
• A new validator consensus model: Instead of recording individual validator votes as on-chain transactions, validators can communicate directly and combine approvals into cryptographic certificates.
• Lower validator voting costs: The new model introduces a flat 0.8 SOL admission fee per epoch, reported to be around 60% cheaper than previous voting costs.
• Changes to network metrics: With voting transactions moved off-chain, headline transaction counts could decline even if actual user demand remains unchanged.

Why this matters:
Quicker transaction finality could strengthen Solana’s suitability for payments, decentralised trading and financial applications that depend on rapid settlement.

However, finality and throughput are different measures. The upgrade changes how quickly transactions become irreversible; it does not directly guarantee an increase in transaction-processing capacity.

For SOL, the activation removes uncertainty around the upgrade’s launch, but future price performance will still depend on market conditions, liquidity and demand.

According to Binance News, citing ChainCatcher, the upgrade is scheduled to activate on the Hoodi testnet on October 26 at 17:42:48 UTC — October 27 at 1:42:48 AM UTC+8.

Key details:
• Block gas limit: Set to rise to 200 million.
• Proposed changes: The upgrade includes enshrined proposer-builder separation, block-level access lists and changes to gas accounting.
• Testing progress: Sepolia activated the upgrade on October 6, ahead of the planned Hoodi activation.
• Node operator action: Operators must update their execution-layer and consensus-layer clients before activation.

The Hoodi testnet activation is another step in testing Ethereum’s proposed network changes. However, an Ethereum mainnet activation date has not yet been set.

Testnet milestones are worth following, but they do not guarantee a specific mainnet timeline or outcome.

Analytics firm Allium reports that stablecoin payments have reached $482 billion so far this year, up 45%.

Several developments are helping connect crypto with traditional payment infrastructure:
• Card spending: Stablecoin-linked card payments are gaining traction.
• Payment networks: Visa and Mastercard are building connections between digital assets and established payment systems.
• Crypto payment rails: Companies such as Stripe are expanding the infrastructure connecting crypto to everyday transactions.

The broader takeaway is that stablecoin adoption cannot be measured by supply alone. Payment volumes and actual usage offer another perspective on how these assets are being used.

As payment infrastructure develops, stablecoins could play a growing role in digital commerce and cross-border money movement. Their long-term impact will depend on adoption, regulation and the reliability of the systems supporting them.

The platform is designed to support four key functions:
• Hold: Manage funds in stablecoins and fiat currencies.
• Convert: Move between different asset types.
• Send: Make global transfers.
• Spend: Access spending options through cards and bank payouts.

By bringing these capabilities together, the partnership highlights how stablecoins are increasingly being explored for payments and money movement beyond crypto trading.

The opportunity lies in connecting digital assets with familiar financial services, while making it easier for users and businesses to manage and move funds across different systems.

As stablecoin payment infrastructure develops, accessibility, regulatory compliance and risk management will remain important considerations.

Announced on October 15, the launch enables businesses to prefund cross-border payouts through Visa Direct using USDC in near real time. Inyo Global is the first platform provider enabling the capability.

What does this mean for payment businesses?
• 24/7 funding: Businesses can prefund payouts with USDC beyond traditional banking funding windows.
• Cross-border money movement: The funds support payouts that can be settled in local currency for recipients.
• Integrated infrastructure: Inyo Global combines onboarding, fraud and compliance processes, payments and payout capabilities through its platform.
• Wider reach: Inyo’s platform supports domestic and international payouts across more than 180 countries.

Importantly, this is a business-focused payment infrastructure development, not a new consumer-facing Visa product.

The shift from pilot to commercial production highlights how stablecoins are increasingly being explored as tools for liquidity management and cross-border settlement, alongside their existing role in crypto markets.

Visa has indicated that it is working with additional clients and partners, although it has not announced a timeline for further integrations or projected transaction volumes.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Ripple has partnered with Arf to bring RLUSD-powered settlement liquidity to the XRP Ledger (XRPL), targeting a key challenge in cross-border payments: access to working capital.

Payment providers often need funds available in different markets before international transfers can be completed. Maintaining that liquidity across multiple countries can tie up capital and create operational challenges.

The partnership aims to address this through:
• Short-term RLUSD funding: Licensed payment companies can access funds for cross-border payment flows.
• Flexible capital deployment: Providers can use the funding and typically repay it within one to five days after payments are completed.
• Existing payment activity: Arf reports approximately $10 billion in annual global settlement volume.
• Potential on-chain lending: Arf plans to explore XRPL’s proposed Single Asset Vaults and Lending Protocol as the network’s native lending infrastructure develops.

The proposed lending features must still pass XRPL’s amendment process before launching on the main network.

This partnership highlights how stablecoins such as RLUSD are being explored as tools for payment liquidity, not just as digital assets for trading.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Solana has activated Alpenglow, its most significant consensus upgrade since 2020.

The mainnet upgrade, activated on October 21, replaces the long-standing TowerBFT consensus system with Votor, a new protocol designed to make transactions final much faster.

Key developments:
• Targeting 150ms finality: The upgrade aims to reduce expected finality from approximately 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds.
• A new validator consensus model: Instead of recording individual validator votes as on-chain transactions, validators can communicate directly and combine approvals into cryptographic certificates.
• Lower validator voting costs: The new model introduces a flat 0.8 SOL admission fee per epoch, reported to be around 60% cheaper than previous voting costs.
• Changes to network metrics: With voting transactions moved off-chain, headline transaction counts could decline even if actual user demand remains unchanged.

Why this matters:
Quicker transaction finality could strengthen Solana’s suitability for payments, decentralised trading and financial applications that depend on rapid settlement.

However, finality and throughput are different measures. The upgrade changes how quickly transactions become irreversible; it does not directly guarantee an increase in transaction-processing capacity.

For SOL, the activation removes uncertainty around the upgrade’s launch, but future price performance will still depend on market conditions, liquidity and demand.

• 24/7 funding: Businesses can prefund payouts with USDC beyond traditional banking funding windows.
• Cross-border money movement: The funds support payouts that can be settled in local currency for recipients.
• Integrated infrastructure: Inyo Global combines onboarding, fraud and compliance processes, payments and payout capabilities through its platform.
• Wider reach: Inyo’s platform supports domestic and international payouts across more than 180 countries.

Importantly, this is a business-focused payment infrastructure development, not a new consumer-facing Visa product.

The shift from pilot to commercial production highlights how stablecoins are increasingly being explored as tools for liquidity management and cross-border settlement, alongside their existing role in crypto markets.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Solana is targeting a major improvement in blockchain transaction finality with its upcoming Alpenglow upgrade.

Scheduled for October 21, 2026, the upgrade aims to reduce transaction finality from approximately 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds, a potential reduction of nearly 99%.

Why does finality matter?
It is the point at which a transaction is considered irreversible by the network. Faster finality could help applications that need confirmation before releasing funds or completing the next step in a transaction.
Potential use cases include:
• Payments: Shorter waits before treating transfers as settled.
• Trading: Faster completion of operations that depend on transaction finality.
• Tokenized assets: More responsive settlement for blockchain-based financial products.
• Financial applications: Better support for workflows that depend on quick, reliable confirmation.
